turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I’ve been making mistakes at work that I really know better than to make. I’m a camera operator and editor, and lately I’ll do things like label camera cards wrong, miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I thought I checked it. It’s happened enough that it kind of scared me.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient reports repeated work errors involving mislabeled camera cards, missed timecode notes, and incorrect lower-thirds despite checking.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking, memory, or concentration besides the mistakes at work?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I’ve noticed it when people are talking to me too. Like on set, a producer will give me a note directly, and I’m looking right at them, but my mind has already jumped ahead to the lens change or the next shot. Then I realize I didn’t actually take in what they said, and I have to ask them to repeat it. It’s embarrassing because I was standing right there.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient reports looking at a producer speaking directly to them but not taking in the note and needing it repeated.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy? Or have you been feeling unusually anxious lately?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so, not in a major way. I mean, I get frustrated and stressed when I mess something up, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless or that I’ve stopped enjoying things. And I’m not walking around feeling anxious all the time.
